newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan rice exports prices seen rising.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan rice exports prices seen rising.

text.p: Pakistani rice export prices are likely to rise moderately this month on expected sales to France, Iraq and Sri Lanka, dealers said on Thursday.

Exporter Khalid Ghori of Matco Rice Processing said France was interested in buying 9,000 tonnes of brown (unpolished) super basmati rice, Sri Lanka 1,000 tonnes of superior basmati and Iraq around 500,000 tonnes of IRRI-6.
"One agent for an importer in France is in the market and has started buying brown rice in local currency," Ghori said.
Sri Lanka importers wanted to buy 1,000 tonnes of superior basmati for shipment before the Sri Lankan government ends a relaxation of import duty on December 25, he said.
He said Iraq was in the market for cheap IRRI-6 and Pakistan was expected to export a substantial quantity to Baghdad following the Iraqi oil-for-food deal with the United Nations.
Pakistan could sell Iraq 500,000 tonnes of an expected exportable surplus of 700,000 tonnes of IRRI-6, Ghori said, estimating Iraq's 1997 needs at more than a million tonnes.
An official of the state-run Rice Export Corporation said the corporation had 30,000 tonnes of IRRI-6 rice which could be sold by open auction in which Iraqi importers could participate.
Javed Islam Agha, chairman of the Rice Exporters Association of Pakistan, said Iraq was unlikely to use all the cash at its disposal to buy Pakistani foodstuffs.
"I think Iraq will not divert all its funds to Pakistan," Agha said. "It will see its priorities."

Iraq's immediate requirements were not high, so rice prices in local markets had not moved abnormally, Agha said. Domestic rice prices had not improved since a 7.86 percent devaluation of the rupee against the dollar on October 22, he said.
Jordanian traders said on Tuesday that Iraq had unfrozen $70 million worth of funds in a deal arranged by an Austrian firm in exchange for substantial commodity purchases.
Exporters said Pakistan's traditional rival India was said to be seeking a big rice deal with Iraq, which usually meets most of its needs from Pakistan, Vietnam and Thailand.

"Thailand is expensive, while Vietnam is unlikely to match quality. It only leaves Pakistan and India in the field," Ghori said, adding that a recent fall in the domestic prices of IRRI-6 was likely to make Pakistani exports more competitive.
"We expect domestic rates to fall as low as $195 per tonne, giving us room to export at current FOB (freight on board) rates of $215 per tonne," he said.
Pakistan's rice output is likely to reach 3.5 million tonnes in 1996/97 (July-June), slightly up on last year's 3.47 million.
Production of IRRI-6 is estimated at 2.27 million tonnes and superior quality basmati at 1.2 million tonnes.
